body_ar:
من المسائل التي يتكلم فيها العلماء مسألة الإيمان، ومذهب السلف أنه قول واعتقاد وعمل، وأن العمل جزء من الإيمان، وقد خالف في العمل بعض السلف، وقد بين الشيخ مرتبة هذا الخلاف وما يترتب عليه.
تعريف الإيمان لغة واصطلاحاً:
قال الناظم: [ذلك والإيمان كل قد شمل عقداً بقلب مع قول وعمل بنية في سنة وبالعمل زيادة ونقصاً المثل احتمل] قوله: (ذلك)، أي: اعرف ذلك، وهذا يسمى الاقتضاب، فبدأ الكلام على توحيد الله سبحانه وتعالى وهو الركن الأول من أركان الإيمان؛ لأن أركان الإيمان ستة هي: الإيمان بالله. والإيمان بملائكته. والإيمان بكتبه. والإيمان برسله. والإيمان باليوم الآخر. والإيمان بالقدر خيره وشره. وقد سبق الكلام على القدر عرضاً في ذكر صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى، وكل ما سوى ذلك فهو داخل في الإيمان بالله سبحانه وتعالى...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Among the questions the scholars discuss is the question of faith. The position of the early generations is that it is utterance, inward conviction and action, and that action is a part of faith. Some of the early generations dissented as regards action, and the Sheikh has set out the rank of this disagreement and what follows from it.

## The definition of faith, in the language and in technical usage

The versifier said: *[That. And faith is a whole that has comprised an assent in the heart together with utterance and action, with intention, in accordance with the sunnah; and through action it has admitted increase and, likewise, decrease.]*

His words "that" mean: know that. This is what is called abrupt transition (iqtiḍāb). He began the discussion with the oneness of God, glorified and exalted is He, which is the first of the pillars of faith — for the pillars of faith are six:

Faith in God.
Faith in His angels.
Faith in His books.
Faith in His messengers.
Faith in the Last Day.
Faith in the divine decree, its good and its ill.

The divine decree has already been discussed in passing, in the course of mentioning the attributes of God, glorified and exalted is He; and everything other than that falls within faith in God, glorified and exalted is He …

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis after the pillars of faith have merely been listed, and never reaches the disagreement over action which the synopsis says the Sheikh sets out. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/L-36.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.arabic: وقد خالف في العمل بعض السلف، وقد بين الشيخ مرتبة هذا الخلاف وما يترتب عليه
flags.context: the closing sentence of the site's synopsis
options: record that the promised treatment is absent from the served text
present the record as containing the Sheikh's treatment of the disagreement
flags.note: The clearest case in this slice of style guide section 10. The synopsis announces both a disagreement — whether action is a constituent part of faith — and the Sheikh's own ruling on where that disagreement stands and what follows from it. The served text reaches neither. It stops after listing the six pillars. A reader arriving at a page titled 'Questions Concerning Faith' would be told in the synopsis that the Sheikh has settled the matter, and would then find no settlement. The question is also among the most consequential in creed, bearing on when a person is judged to have left the faith, so an English page that appears to give his position and does not is a real hazard. Suppress or banner prominently.

flags.arabic: ذلك والإيمان كل قد شمل عقداً بقلب مع قول وعمل / بنية في سنة وبالعمل زيادة ونقصاً المثل احتمل
flags.context: the quoted lines of the versified base text
options: That. And faith is a whole that has comprised an assent in the heart together with utterance and action, with intention, in accordance with the sunnah; and through action it has admitted increase and, likewise, decrease.
…and by action it has borne increase and decrease alike.
…and with action, increase and its like in decrease are admitted.
flags.note: The second line is genuinely hard and the English is provisional. 'المثل احتمل' with 'زيادة ونقصاً' most naturally means that the two are admitted alike — that faith increases and decreases in the same way and by the same cause, namely action. A weaker reading would take 'المثل' as the subject of 'احتمل'. The line matters because it states the position that faith admits of increase and decrease, which is the very point of disagreement the synopsis announces. It should be checked against the base text before publication rather than taken from this rendering.

flags.context: the definition of faith in the quoted verse, against the synopsis's wording
options: an assent in the heart together with utterance and action
a binding of the heart together with speech and deed
conviction of the heart with word and work
flags.note: The verse orders the three as heart, utterance, action; the synopsis orders them as utterance, conviction, action. The English preserves each order as its own source gives it and does not harmonise them. 'عقد' is the act of binding the heart to a thing, which is why the noun 'عقيدة' is formed from it; 'assent' keeps that, where 'belief' would blur it into the whole of faith, which is what is being defined.

flags.context: the rhetorical term the Sheikh applies to the word 'ذلك'
flags.note: A technical term of Arabic rhetoric for moving to a new subject without a connective easing the passage, as against 'takhalluṣ', where the transition is made smoothly. It is not in the glossary. Given with the Arabic in brackets on the house convention, since the English is a description rather than an established equivalent.

translator_notes: One of a run of fifteen records, IDs 707-721, in the written-creed section, all uploaded on 9 and 10 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/L-* series, numbered L-26 to L-39 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lesson was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The base text being commented on is identified inside this run. Record 719 has the Sheikh speaking of 'completing the commentary on the Sheikh's versification', and of that versifier's rendering of Khalil's Jāmiʿ in some five hundred lines; record 716 describes the base text as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq whose opening section is on creed; and record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. Taken together these settle that 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him' in this run is the living author of the versified base text and not the lecturer. The author is never named.

This record introduces the quoted lines with 'قال الناظم', 'the versifier said', where the rest of the run has 'قال الشيخ حفظه الله'. That is part of what settles the referent: the two formulas mark the same base text.

'القدر خيره وشره' is rendered 'the divine decree, its good and its ill'. The glossary flags qaḍāʾ/qadar as a pairing pending addition (style guide section 13); here only 'قدر' occurs and it is the standard sixth pillar, so no new rendering has been coined.
The English sets the six pillars as a list where the source separates them with full stops on one line, which is how the source itself presents them. No word has been added.
